channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Germany's Four Major Foundations Cease Operations in Georgia Amidst Political Disputes
item.description: Germany's four major political foundations have closed their Tbilisi offices following disputes with the ruling Georgian Dream party over new grant regulations. The German ambassador blamed the Georgian government's decisions for forcing the foundations to suspend work, impacting Georgia's European integration efforts. Government pressure on foreign-funded organizations has been escalating since 2024.

item.title: Kremlin Spokesperson Accuses Europe of Seeking to Prolong Ukraine War
item.description: Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov accused European countries of aiming to prolong the war in Ukraine, contrasting their approach with that of the United States. Peskov stated that Europe is making every effort to extend the conflict and could potentially obstruct peace agreement efforts. His remarks were made during a press briefing on Wednesday, October 14.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Finance Minister Explains Benefits of Large Loan from China
item.description: Kazakhstan's Finance Minister, Madhi Takiev, addressed concerns about rising state debt during a Kurultai session. He explained that while debt servicing costs are projected to increase, they remain manageable within the budget. Takiev stated that the current national debt is 38.5 trillion tenge.

item.title: Afghan Red Crescent Society and UK Envoy Discuss Humanitarian Aid for Vulnerable Afghans
item.description: The president of the Afghan Red Crescent Society (ARCS), Shahabuddin Delawar, met with UK Special Representative for Afghanistan, Richard Lindsay, to discuss the humanitarian situation and expanding aid for vulnerable communities. Discussions focused on support for victims of natural disasters, Afghan returnees, and other vulnerable groups.

item.title: Central Asia Strengthens Transboundary Water Cooperation with New Equipment and Training
item.description: The International Water Management Institute (IWMI) conducted a mission to the Isfara River basin, spanning Tajikistan, Kyrgyzstan, and Uzbekistan. The initiative aims to improve water resource management by providing modern monitoring equipment and enhancing the capacity of local water organizations. This effort, part of the Blue Peace Central Asia project, seeks to foster practical cooperation between the three nations to address challenges in shared water resource management.

item.title: Astana Hosts Meeting on Transport Issues for ECO Member States
item.description: Senior officials convened in Astana to prepare for the 14th Council of Transport Ministers of the Economic Cooperation Organization (ECO). Participants reviewed draft strategies for sustainable transport development and adaptation to external challenges for 2026-2035, and the Astana Declaration. Kazakhstan emphasized the importance of developing international transport corridors and improving logistics efficiency, highlighting the Trans-Caspian route and the Kazakhstan-Turkmenistan-Iran corridor.

item.title: Uzbekistan's National Postal Operator UzPost Transferred to Trust Management by Wildberries
item.description: Uzbekistan's national postal operator, UzPost, has transferred its state-owned shares to WB INT EXPORT LLC, a subsidiary of Russia's Wildberries marketplace, for trust management. This decision was made during a shareholders' meeting on September 21. The agreement grants WB INT EXPORT LLC, as the trust manager, all shareholder rights, including the nomination of five members to UzPost's nine-member supervisory board.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Provide State-Funded Lawyers for Children Affected by Violence
item.description: Children in Uzbekistan who are victims of violence will be provided with lawyers at state expense. Children who witness violence will also have the right to legal assistance from the state. These changes were established in a new law signed by the president.

item.title: Mongolia Expresses Readiness to Expand Cooperation with Uzbekistan Across All Sectors
item.description: Mongolia is ready to expand cooperation with Uzbekistan in all areas, according to the national news agency "Montsame". A meeting between parliamentary delegations discussed strengthening trade, economic, social, cultural, and educational ties, as well as legislative experience exchange.

item.title: Russian Rapper NAVAI Arrested at Kazakhstan Border with Drugs
item.description: Russian rapper NAVAI, known by his stage name, was detained at the "Korday" border crossing point entering Kazakhstan. Police found and confiscated drugs during a search of his vehicle. A criminal case for drug smuggling has been initiated, and the suspect has been placed in a temporary detention facility. His planned concert in Astana was canceled due to technical reasons.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Assess Family Income for Funeral Payments from 2027
item.description: Starting in 2027, eligibility for a one-time funeral payment in Kazakhstan will be determined based on the applicant's social well-being level, according to an order from the Minister of Labor and Social Protection. A digital family card will be used to assess financial status. Applicants categorized as having a high social well-being level may be denied the payment.

item.title: Singer Navai Detained in Kazakhstan on Drug Smuggling Charges; Astana Concert Canceled
item.description: Russian singer Navai was detained in the Zhambyl region of Kazakhstan near the border with Kyrgyzstan on suspicion of drug smuggling. Police found and seized narcotics in his vehicle. A criminal case has been initiated, and the singer is in temporary detention. His scheduled concert in Astana on October 14 was canceled due to "technical reasons."

item.title: Taliban Foreign Minister Meets Indian Chargé d’Affaires to Discuss Bilateral Ties
item.description: Taliban Foreign Minister Amir Khan Muttaqi met with Indian Chargé d’Affaires Yatin Patel in Kabul to discuss strengthening bilateral relations and expanding economic cooperation. Muttaqi emphasized the growing trade between Afghanistan and India and the need for public and private sector collaboration. Patel affirmed India's desire to enhance engagement in economic, political, and humanitarian fields.

item.title: Singer Navai Detained in Kazakhstan on Drug Smuggling Charges
item.description: Singer Navai was detained in Kazakhstan on October 13 at the "Korday" border crossing while entering the country, on suspicion of drug smuggling. Police discovered and seized narcotics in the vehicle the performer was traveling in. The detention occurred as he crossed the border into Kazakhstan.

item.title: Global Diesel Shortage Could Last Until 2027, International Energy Agency Warns
item.description: Supply disruptions from Russia and the Middle East are depleting global diesel reserves, warns the International Energy Agency (IEA). Even with refinery recovery by year-end, replenishing stocks will be slow. The IEA predicts a tight market through the first half of 2027, impacting prices and economic activity worldwide.

item.title: Almaty School Switches to Remote Learning After Mass Food Poisoning Incident
item.description: The Republican Physics and Mathematics School in Almaty has temporarily moved to distance learning following a mass food poisoning incident. The Ministry of Education stated that sanitary violations were found in the cafeteria. A monitoring group is investigating the circumstances, and the school administration has been instructed to enhance food safety controls.

item.title: Construction Begins on 5,000-Seat Multipurpose Sports Complex in Aktobe
item.description: Construction has commenced on a new multipurpose sports complex in Aktobe, designed to accommodate 5,000 spectators. The facility will host major competitions and events, featuring a central arena, swimming pool, and various sports halls. Regional Governor Askhat Shakhanov emphasized the project's alignment with national goals to develop sports infrastructure and promote active lifestyles.

item.title: China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan Railway: Enhancing Local Economic Benefits Beyond Transit
item.description: The China-Kyrgyzstan-Uzbekistan railway project, under construction since December 2024, requires integrated transport corridor development to generate local economic benefits. Uzbekistan's President Mirziyoyev stressed the need for logistics hubs and service centers. Ensuring small shippers can utilize the railway and minimizing border delays are crucial for maximizing economic impact in Kyrgyzstan and Uzbekistan.

item.title: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev Arrives in Baku for CICA Summit
item.description: Kazakh President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has arrived in Baku for a working visit to attend the 7th Summit of the Conference on Interaction and Confidence Building Measures in Asia (CICA). He was welcomed at Baku airport by Azerbaijani Deputy Prime Minister Samir Sharifov. The summit focuses on regional cooperation and security.

item.title: UNHCR Supports Afghan Returnees in Establishing Businesses and Creating Jobs
item.description: The UNHCR is assisting Afghans returning to their country by helping them start businesses and create employment opportunities. This initiative also provides jobs for women returnees and internally displaced people, amid ongoing deportations from neighboring countries.

item.title: Auditors Identify Risks in Budget Planning for 456 Billion Tenge
item.description: Auditors have identified risks in the planning of the republican budget for 2027-2029, amounting to 456 billion tenge. These risks were eliminated based on recommendations from the Supreme Audit Chamber. The preliminary assessment revealed shortcomings in expenditure planning.

item.title: Tokayev Arrives in Baku for CICA Summit to Discuss Asian Security and Cooperation
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has arrived in Baku for the 7th Summit of the Conference on Interaction and Confidence-Building Measures in Asia (CICA). The summit will focus on security, trust-building, transport links, digitalization, and sustainable economic growth in Asia.

item.title: Tokayev Attends CICA Summit in Baku
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev is participating in the 7th summit of the Conference on Interaction and Confidence-Building Measures in Asia (CICA) in Baku. The summit aims to discuss security and cooperation among Asian nations.

item.title: Kazakh President Tokayev Arrives in Azerbaijan for Working Visit
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has arrived in Baku for a working visit to attend the 7th Summit of the Conference on Interaction and Confidence Building Measures in Asia (CICA). He was met at the airport by Azerbaijan's Deputy Prime Minister Samir Sharifov. The summit aims to strengthen cooperation for peace, security, and stability in Asia.

item.title: Ukraine Targets Russia's Largest Data Center with Drone Attack
item.description: International media reports indicate Ukraine has targeted Russia's largest data center, "Balakovo," owned by Sberbank, with a drone attack. This follows previous attacks on Yandex data centers. Sberbank confirmed the attack but stated all systems are operational. The "Balakovo" center was reportedly slated to host Russia's largest supercomputer by 2027.

item.title: Kazakh President Arrives in Baku for CICA Summit
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev has arrived in Baku for a working visit to attend the 7th Summit of the Conference on Interaction and Confidence Building Measures in Asia (CICA). The summit, chaired by Azerbaijan, aims to strengthen dialogue and mutual trust among Asian countries, discussing regional security, stability, and sustainable development.

item.title: Over 2kg of Illicit Opium Seized in Uzbekistan; Attackers Injure Three
item.description: Authorities in Samarqand and Farg‘ona have seized over 2 kilograms of illicit opium. During the operation, a woman, her three sons, and son-in-law attempted to sell drugs and attacked buyers with cold weapons, causing serious injuries to three people. Investigations are ongoing.

item.title: Three Arrested in Samarqand for Attempting to Sell Counterfeit US Dollars
item.description: Authorities in Samarqand have arrested three individuals attempting to sell $7,400 in counterfeit US dollars brought from Turkey. The suspects, aged 30, 24, and 23, were apprehended by the State Security Service, Ministry of Internal Affairs, and customs officials. An investigation is underway.

item.title: Kazakhstan Dismantles Cross-Border 'Drop Farm' Network for Online Casinos
item.description: Kazakhstan's Financial Monitoring Agency has disrupted criminal groups operating a cross-border 'drop farm' network for online casinos. The scheme involved using bank accounts of citizens from Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, and Kyrgyzstan to process transactions totaling 9.8 billion tenge. Several arrests were made.

item.title: Taliban Detains 26 in Panjshir After Attack on Convoy, Spokesperson Denies Arrests
item.description: Reports indicate Taliban forces detained 26 individuals in Panjshir province following an attack on a Taliban convoy. However, the Taliban governor's spokesman in Panjshir denied the arrests, stating the incident is under investigation. Analysts discussed the situation.

item.title: Tajik President Extends Moratorium on Business Inspections for Two Years
item.description: Tajik President Emomali Rahmon has extended the moratorium on business inspections for an additional two years. Effective until January 1, 2029, no entity except tax authorities can inspect businesses. This decision was announced during a meeting with investors and entrepreneurs in Dushanbe. The president has instructed relevant bodies to monitor compliance with the moratorium.

item.title: Kazakhstan Changes Procedure for Pension and Funeral Benefit Applications
item.description: Kazakhstan is altering the procedures for processing pension payments and one-time funeral allowances. The new rules allow citizens to apply for age-related pensions, state basic pension payments, and savings from the Unified Accumulative Pension Fund with a single application. Corrections to applications are allowed within specified timeframes.

item.title: UNICEF: Denying Girls Education Hinders Pregnant Women's Healthcare Access in Afghanistan
item.description: UNICEF reports that restrictions on girls' education and women's work in Afghanistan's health sector have impeded pregnant women and mothers' access to medical care. The country faces high neonatal mortality rates, with many mothers dying from pregnancy-related causes. Denying girls education and restricting female healthcare workers limits essential prenatal and maternal services.

item.title: Inflation Erodes Revenue Growth for Kazakh Cafes and Restaurants
item.description: Kazakhstan's cafes and restaurants saw a 16% revenue increase, but after accounting for inflation, only 3.2% real growth remains. This marks the lowest real growth in six years. Almaty and Astana, the largest cities, experienced significant slowdowns in real growth.

item.title: Nearly 1,500 Illegal Devices Disrupting Mobile Communication Quality in Uzbekistan Shut Down
item.description: Uzbekistan's "Uzkomnazorat" inspection has shut down approximately 1,500 illegal devices negatively impacting mobile communication quality. During the first nine months of the year, 179 control measures were conducted, resulting in administrative penalties for 85 officials.

item.title: Tajikistan and Iran Abolish Visa Regime for Land and Third-Country Travel
item.description: Tajikistan and Iran have abolished their visa regime for travel via land routes and through third countries. Previously, citizens of both nations could only travel visa-free by air. This agreement simplifies travel and strengthens bilateral relations between the two countries.

item.title: Uzbek President Mirziyoyev Departs for Azerbaijan to Attend SCO Summit
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev has departed for Azerbaijan to participate in the seventh summit of the Conference on Interaction and Confidence-Building Measures in Asia. The summit will focus on cooperation and confidence-building measures within the region.

item.title: UNICEF Reports Over 2.6 Million Afghan Girls Denied Education Since 2021
item.description: UNICEF announced that over 2.6 million girls in Afghanistan have been denied education since 2021. The restrictions have limited learning opportunities, forcing many girls to stay home after sixth grade. This denial impacts their psychological well-being, increasing feelings of isolation and hopelessness. UNICEF continues to support educational programs for both girls and boys.

item.title: Russia Attacks Ukraine's Energy Infrastructure After US President's 'Energy Truce' Announcement
item.description: Russian forces launched strikes on Kyiv overnight, resulting in casualties and damage to residential buildings and energy infrastructure. The attacks occurred after US President Biden announced an 'energy truce'. Several Ukrainian regions reported damage to energy facilities and civilian infrastructure due to missile and drone strikes.

item.title: OIC Envoy Briefs Kabul Diplomats on Afghanistan Visit Outcomes
item.description: The Organization of Islamic Cooperation's Special Envoy to Afghanistan, Ambassador Dr. Tarig Ali Bakheet, briefed ambassadors in Kabul on his recent visit. Discussions focused on humanitarian aid, counter-terrorism, healthcare, education, and livelihood improvements. Bakheet stressed the need for coordinated OIC member state efforts to support Afghanistan's humanitarian and development needs amidst ongoing challenges.
